name: MX1508 dual DC motor driver
description: Mixic MX1508 dual H-bridge (P/N-channel MOSFET) driver for two small brushed DC motors or one bipolar stepper: forward, reverse, brake or coast per motor, about 1.5 A continuous (2 A peak) per channel, thermal shutdown, internal input pull-downs. One supply of 2.4-7.2 V feeds both the bridges and the logic. Sold as: MX1508 2-channel DC motor driver module (red 24.7 x 21 mm board with two 100 uF capacitors, pads + - IN1 IN2 IN3 IN4 on one edge, MOTOR-A and MOTOR-B pads on the other).
eli5: Lets your board make two small motors spin forwards or backwards, using a battery for the motors' power.

pins.description: Supply +, 2.4-7.2 V: feeds the motor bridges (VDD1/VDD2) directly and the chip's logic supply (VCC1/VCC2) through R1/D1. Use a battery or supply that can deliver the motor current. Keep it at 5 V or less when driving the inputs from 3.3 V logic (input high needs 0.6 x VCC)
Ground: shared by the motor supply and the microcontroller

pins.name: IN1
pins.description: Motor A input A (INA1): high with IN2 low = forward; PWM for speed. Internal ~15 kOhm pull-down; never above the + supply

pins.name: IN2
pins.description: Motor A input B (INB1): high with IN1 low = reverse; both high = brake, both low = standby/coast

pins.name: IN3
pins.description: Motor B input A (INA2): high with IN4 low = forward

pins.name: IN4
pins.description: Motor B input B (INB2): high with IN3 low = reverse

pins.name: MOTOR-A1
pins.description: Motor A output pad 1 (one of the two MOTOR-A pads); connect the motor, not the microcontroller

pins.name: MOTOR-B1
pins.description: Motor B output pad 1 (one of the two MOTOR-B pads); connect the motor, not the microcontroller

supplierQuery: MX1508 2 channel DC motor driver module
buildNotes: Truth table (MX1508 datasheet): IN-A high / IN-B low = forward, IN-A low / IN-B high = reverse, both high = brake, both low = standby (outputs off, motor coasts). Motor A = IN1/IN2, motor B = IN3/IN4.

Speed: hold one input high and PWM the other at 10-50 kHz (datasheet PWM mode B, speed follows the duty closely); the motor is driven while the PWM pin is LOW. PWMing one input with the other low (mode A) also works but is less linear.

The board has only one supply (+ and -): + feeds the motors directly and the chip's logic supply through R1/D1. Datasheet: motor supply 2-9.6 V, logic supply 7 V absolute max; the module is documented for 2.4-7.2 V, so stay inside that.

Input high needs 0.6 x VCC. From a 3.3 V ESP32 or Pico keep + at 5 V or less (USB 5 V, 4 x NiMH, 1-2 cell Li-ion with care); 5 V microcontrollers are fine up to 7.2 V. Inputs must never be higher than the + supply.
Join the module's - to the microcontroller GND. Power motors from a battery or 5 V supply, not the 3V3 pin.
Pads are on two edges (supply and inputs on one, MOTOR-A/MOTOR-B on the other): solder header pins or wires and connect with jumper leads.
Small toy/gear motors only (about 1.5 A per channel continuous). A stalled motor heats the chip until its thermal shutdown (about 150 C) cuts the outputs.
If a motor spins the wrong way, swap its two wires at the MOTOR pads.
Some boards sold as MX1508 carry a TC1508A or similar clone chip with the same pins and truth table.

driver.code:
# MX1508 dual brushed-DC motor driver (Mixic MX1508), MicroPython driver for ONE channel (one DC motor).
# Make one MX1508 object per motor: on the red module, motor A = IN1, IN2; motor B = IN3, IN4.
# Logic truth table from the MX1508 datasheet (INAx, INBx -> OUTAx, OUTBx):
#   L, L -> Z, Z   standby: outputs off, motor coasts (also the state with inputs left open:
#                  each input has an internal pull-down of about 15 kOhm)
#   H, L -> H, L   forward
#   L, H -> L, H   reverse
#   H, H -> L, L   brake (motor shorted through the low-side MOSFETs)
# Speed (datasheet "PWM mode B", recommended): hold one input high and PWM the other; the bridge
# switches between driving and braking, so speed follows the duty cycle closely. Forward = INA high,
# PWM on INB; the motor is driven while INB is LOW, so INB's duty is (100 - speed) %.
# The datasheet recommends a PWM frequency of 10-50 kHz for mode B.
# "PWM mode A" (PWM one input, the other low; drive/standby, fast decay) is available with decay='fast',
# but the datasheet notes speed is not accurately set by the duty cycle in this mode.
# Inputs: high >= 0.6 x VCC, low <= 0.6 V, never above VCC.
from machine import Pin, PWM


class MX1508:
    def __init__(self, in_a, in_b, freq=20000, decay='slow'):
        """in_a, in_b: GPIO numbers wired to the channel's two inputs (IN1/IN2 or IN3/IN4).
        freq: PWM frequency for speed control (datasheet: 10-50 kHz).
        decay: 'slow' (PWM mode B, default) or 'fast' (PWM mode A)."""
        self._na = in_a
        self._nb = in_b
        self._freq = freq
        self._decay = decay
        self._pwm = None
        self._a = Pin(in_a, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self._b = Pin(in_b, Pin.OUT, value=0)

    def _release_pwm(self):
        if self._pwm is not None:
            self._pwm.deinit()
            self._pwm = None
            self._a = Pin(self._na, Pin.OUT, value=0)
            self._b = Pin(self._nb, Pin.OUT, value=0)

    def _set(self, va, vb):
        self._release_pwm()
        self._a.value(va)
        self._b.value(vb)

    def _run(self, drive_pin, other_pin, speed, forward):
        # drive_pin is the input that is HIGH for this direction (INA forward, INB reverse).
        speed = max(0, min(100, speed))
        if speed >= 100:
            if forward:
                self._set(1, 0)
            else:
                self._set(0, 1)
            return
        if speed <= 0:
            self.coast()
            return
        self._release_pwm()
        if self._decay == 'fast':
            # Mode A: other input low, PWM the driving input, duty = speed.
            Pin(other_pin, Pin.OUT, value=0)
            self._pwm = PWM(Pin(drive_pin), freq=self._freq, duty_u16=speed * 65535 // 100)
        else:
            # Mode B: driving input held high, PWM the other one; it brakes while high.
            Pin(drive_pin, Pin.OUT, value=1)
            self._pwm = PWM(Pin(other_pin), freq=self._freq, duty_u16=(100 - speed) * 65535 // 100)

    def forward(self, speed=100):
        """OUTA high, OUTB low. speed 0-100 %."""
        self._run(self._na, self._nb, speed, True)

    def reverse(self, speed=100):
        """OUTA low, OUTB high. speed 0-100 %."""
        self._run(self._nb, self._na, speed, False)

    def drive(self, speed):
        """Signed speed -100..100: positive = forward, negative = reverse, 0 = coast."""
        if speed >= 0:
            self.forward(speed)
        else:
            self.reverse(-speed)

    def brake(self):
        """Both inputs high: both outputs low, the motor stops quickly."""
        self._set(1, 1)

    def coast(self):
        """Both inputs low: standby, outputs high-impedance, the motor spins down freely."""
        self._set(0, 0)

    def stop(self):
        self.coast()

example.code:
import time
from mx1508 import MX1508

motor_a = MX1508({IN1}, {IN2})   # motor A on IN1, IN2
while True:
    motor_a.forward()
    print('motor A forward')
    time.sleep(1)
    motor_a.reverse()
    print('motor A reverse')
    time.sleep(1)
    motor_a.coast()
    print('motor A coasting')
    time.sleep(1)
